recipes.title: Soylent Green Smoothie
recipes.description: A vibrant green smoothie packed with spinach, banana, and matcha that delivers a nourishing jolt of energy. This creamy, earthy blend is a wholesome take on the mysterious processed food from the 1973 sci-fi classic. Bright, refreshing, and thankfully made from entirely known ingredients.
recipes.story: The film Soylent Green (1973) imagines a future where food is manufactured from mysterious ingredients. This healthy drink references the movie's cautionary tale about processed food.
instructions: Add the coconut water and spinach to a blender and blend until the spinach is fully broken down.
Add the frozen banana, matcha powder, and protein powder.
Blend on high for 60 seconds until completely smooth and creamy.
Taste and add honey if you prefer a sweeter smoothie.
Add ice cubes and blend briefly to chill.
Pour into two glasses and serve immediately.

recipes.title: Nutrient Bars
recipes.description: Chewy, satisfying no-bake protein bars loaded with oats, peanut butter, honey, and dried fruit. These compact rations are inspired by the survival bars that sustain characters in Snowpiercer and Parable of the Sower. They taste far better than anything you'd find at the back of the train.
recipes.source: Inspired by Snowpiercer & Octavia Butler's Parable of the Sower
recipes.story: In Snowpiercer and Octavia Butler's Parable of the Sower, characters survive on protein bars. The bars represent adaptation to scarcity.
instructions: Line an 8x8-inch baking pan with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, combine the rolled oats, dried fruit, sunflower seeds, and chia seeds.
Warm the peanut butter and honey together in a small saucepan over low heat, stirring until smooth.
Stir in the vanilla extract and salt.
Pour the wet mixture over the dry ingredients and mix thoroughly until everything is well coated.
Press the mixture firmly and evenly into the prepared pan.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours until set, then cut into 12 bars.
Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to one week.

recipes.title: Mung Bean Soup
recipes.description: A fragrant, creamy soup of tender mung beans simmered in coconut milk with ginger, garlic, and turmeric. Inspired by the bland institutional meals in Atwood's Oryx and Crake, this version is anything but dull. Finished with fresh cilantro, it is warming and deeply satisfying.
recipes.source: Inspired by Margaret Atwood's Oryx and Crake
recipes.story: In Margaret Atwood's Oryx and Crake, the Paradice Project serves bland vegan meals to researchers. Food in Atwood's dystopias reflects corporate control over nature.

ingredients.name: dried mung beans, soaked overnight and drained

instructions: Heat coconut oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté the onion until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger, and turmeric and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the drained mung beans, coconut milk, and vegetable broth.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 25-30 minutes until the beans are very tender.
Use an immersion blender to partially blend, leaving some texture.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Ladle into bowls and garnish generously with fresh cilantro.

recipes.title: Kibble Cakes
recipes.description: Crispy, savoury patties made from a scrappy mix of ground meat, grated carrots, and cooked quinoa, seasoned with warm spices. Inspired by the improvised rations of Mad Max: Fury Road, these resourceful little cakes prove that survival food can still be delicious.
recipes.source: Inspired by Mad Max: Fury Road
recipes.story: Inspired by Mad Max: Fury Road, these savoury cakes are made from whatever protein and grain are available. The improvised rations evoke post-apocalyptic resourcefulness.
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the ground meat, cooked quinoa, grated carrot, and beaten egg.
Add the cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder, salt, and pepper and mix until evenly combined.
Form the mixture into 8 small patties, about 1/2-inch thick.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook the patties for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through.
Drain briefly on paper towels and serve hot.

recipes.title: Lab-Grown "Steak"
recipes.description: A hearty plant-based steak made from seasoned seitan, steamed until firm and then seared to a gorgeous crust. Basted in a smoky soy glaze, this futuristic protein delivers satisfying chew and deep umami flavour worthy of a cyberpunk noir dinner.
recipes.story: Near-future fiction like William Gibson's Neuromancer features synthetic meat. Speculative fiction explores the ethics of lab-grown foods.
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together the vital wheat gluten, nutritional yeast, smoked paprika, garlic powder, and black pepper.
Add the soy sauce, olive oil, and vegetable broth and stir until a dough forms, then knead for 2 minutes.
Divide the dough into 4 portions and shape each into a steak-like oval about 3/4-inch thick.
Place the steaks in a steamer basket and steam for 25 minutes until firm.
Heat vegetable oil in a cast-iron skillet over high heat.
Sear each steak for 2-3 minutes per side until a deep golden crust forms.
Baste with additional soy sauce while searing for extra flavour.
Let rest for 2 minutes, then serve sliced on the bias.

recipes.title: Victory Gin
recipes.description: A stark, stripped-down gin drink with just a whisper of sweetness and the warm bite of clove. George Orwell's bleak dystopia called for harsh spirits, and this austere cocktail captures that oppressive simplicity. Sip it slowly and be grateful you have better options.
recipes.story: In George Orwell's 1984, citizens drink harsh Victory gin as part of rationing. The acrid drink underlines the bleakness of the regime.
instructions: Pour the gin into a plain tumbler.
Add the cold water and stir to combine.
Drop in the sugar and stir until dissolved.
Add the whole clove and let it steep for a moment.
Serve neat or over a single ice cube, and drink as Big Brother watches.

recipes.title: Victory Coffee
recipes.description: A thin, barely sweetened chicory coffee that captures the deprivation of Orwell's Oceania. Brewed weak on purpose, this austere cup is a reminder of what rationing does to life's small pleasures. Pair it with a Victory Gin if you dare.
recipes.story: The novel 1984 also mentions thin Victory coffee. The tasteless coffee emphasises deprivation.
instructions: Bring the water to a boil and let it cool for 30 seconds.
Place the chicory coffee grounds in a mug or French press.
Pour the hot water over the grounds and let steep for 3-4 minutes.
Strain if necessary and add the scant half-teaspoon of sugar.
Stir once and drink without further embellishment.

recipes.title: Instant Ramen
recipes.description: A rich, steaming bowl of miso ramen topped with a perfectly marinated soft-boiled egg, sliced roast pork, and fresh scallions. Inspired by the neon-lit noodle stands of Blade Runner, this bowl is the kind of soul-warming meal you'd crave in a rain-soaked cyberpunk cityscape.
recipes.story: Cyberpunk settings like Blade Runner feature noodle stands. The dish blends Eastern and Western influences in futuristic cities.
instructions: Bring the broth to a simmer in a medium pot.
Whisk in the miso paste and soy sauce until fully dissolved.
Cook the ramen noodles in the broth according to package directions, about 3 minutes.
Divide the noodles and broth between two deep bowls.
Top each bowl with sliced roast pork, a halved soft-boiled egg, and sliced scallions.
Drizzle with sesame oil and tuck a sheet of nori alongside.
Serve immediately while steaming hot.

recipes.title: Protein Skewers
recipes.description: Grilled skewers of marinated tofu drenched in a rich peanut sauce with bright hits of lime and chili. Inspired by the Belter street food of The Expanse, these skewers are sustainable, flavourful, and perfect for eating with your hands while floating through the asteroid belt.
recipes.source: Inspired by James S.A. Corey's The Expanse
recipes.story: In James S.A. Corey's The Expanse, Belters eat skewers of insect protein. Such foods highlight sustainability and resourcefulness in space.

ingredients.name: block (14 oz) extra-firm tofu, pressed and cubed

instructions: Whisk together the peanut butter, soy sauce, lime juice, sriracha, sesame oil, and warm water to make a smooth sauce.
Toss the tofu cubes in half of the peanut sauce and marinate for at least 15 minutes.
Thread the marinated tofu onto soaked wooden skewers.
Preheat a grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Grill the skewers for 3-4 minutes per side until nicely charred.
Serve with the remaining peanut sauce for dipping and lime wedges on the side.

recipes.title: Soma Cocktail
recipes.description: A soothing, floral herbal drink inspired by the happiness-inducing soma of Aldous Huxley's Brave New World. This calming blend of chamomile, lavender, and honey creates a gentle, dreamy beverage that soothes the senses without any dystopian side effects.
recipes.source: Inspired by Aldous Huxley's Brave New World
recipes.story: In Brave New World, soma is the government-issued drug that keeps citizens blissfully compliant. This gentle herbal drink channels that idea of enforced tranquillity into a harmless, fragrant cup.
instructions: Bring the water to a boil in a small saucepan.
Remove from heat and add the chamomile tea bags and dried lavender.
Steep for 5 minutes, then remove the tea bags and strain out the lavender.
Stir in the honey until fully dissolved.
Add the lemon juice and stir gently.
Pour into two cups and garnish with a fresh mint sprig. Serve warm or chilled over ice.

recipes.title: Fahrenheit 451 Burnt Ends
recipes.description: Tender, smoky barbecue burnt ends with a caramelised crust of spice and sauce. Named with a wink at Ray Bradbury's novel about book burning, these richly flavoured beef brisket cubes are slow-cooked until they practically melt. The only thing burning here is delicious.
recipes.story: Fahrenheit 451 envisions a world where firemen burn books instead of saving them. These BBQ burnt ends playfully invert the destruction, turning fire into something nourishing and irresistible.
instructions: Preheat oven to 275 degrees F.
Combine the smoked paprika, brown sugar, garlic powder, cayenne, black pepper, and salt in a bowl.
Toss the brisket cubes in the spice rub until evenly coated.
Spread the cubes in a single layer on a wire rack set over a baking sheet.
Cook for 3 hours until the exterior is dark and crusty.
Transfer the cubes to a foil-lined baking dish, toss with BBQ sauce, butter, and beef broth.
Cover tightly with foil and return to the oven for 1 hour until the meat is fork-tender.
Serve piled high with extra sauce on the side.

recipes.title: Snowpiercer Protein Blocks
recipes.description: Dense, nutty energy squares made with cricket flour, oats, and dark chocolate chips. Inspired by the mysterious protein blocks fed to the tail-section passengers of Snowpiercer, this version is far more appetizing and packed with genuine nutrition.
recipes.story: In Snowpiercer, the impoverished tail-section passengers survive on gelatinous protein blocks made from ground insects. The reveal of their origin is one of the film's most memorable and disturbing moments.
instructions: Preheat oven to 325 degrees F and line an 8x8-inch pan with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, combine the oats, cricket flour (or almond flour), cinnamon, and salt.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the maple syrup, melted coconut oil, and peanut butter until smooth.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry and stir until well combined.
Fold in the dark chocolate chips.
Press the mixture firmly into the prepared pan.
Bake for 18-20 minutes until the edges are golden.
Let cool completely in the pan before cutting into 16 squares.

recipes.title: The Road's Canned Peaches
recipes.description: Warm, cinnamon-spiced peaches served over vanilla ice cream or yogurt, inspired by the unforgettable scene in Cormac McCarthy's The Road. In the novel, finding a can of peaches is a rare moment of grace. This simple dessert celebrates that sweetness.
recipes.source: Inspired by Cormac McCarthy's The Road
recipes.story: In The Road, a father and son wandering through a post-apocalyptic wasteland discover a cache of canned goods. The peaches they share become a transcendent moment of hope and humanity amid total desolation.

ingredients.name: (15 oz each) sliced peaches in syrup, drained
Vanilla ice cream or Greek yogurt for serving

instructions: Melt the butter in a medium skillet over medium heat.
Add the brown sugar and cinnamon, stirring until the sugar dissolves and bubbles.
Add the drained peach slices and toss gently to coat.
Cook for 5-7 minutes, turning occasionally, until the peaches are warmed through and lightly caramelised.
Remove from heat and stir in the vanilla extract and nutmeg.
Spoon the warm peaches over vanilla ice cream or Greek yogurt and serve immediately.

recipes.title: Handmaid's Tale Red Velvet Cake
recipes.description: A striking, deeply crimson red velvet layer cake with tangy cream cheese frosting. The vivid red colour evokes the handmaids' cloaks in Margaret Atwood's chilling novel, turning a symbol of oppression into something celebratory and indulgent. Rich, moist, and unforgettable.
recipes.source: Inspired by Margaret Atwood's The Handmaid's Tale
recipes.story: In The Handmaid's Tale, the colour red is inescapable, worn by the handmaids as a mark of their subjugation. This red velvet cake reclaims the symbolism, transforming it into an act of sweetness and defiance.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F and grease and flour two 9-inch round cake pans.
Whisk together the flour, sugar, baking soda, salt, and cocoa powder in a large bowl.
In a separate bowl, combine the oil, buttermilk, eggs, red food colouring, vanilla, and vinegar.
Add the wet ingredients to the dry and mix until just combined and smooth.
Divide the batter evenly between the prepared pans.
Bake for 28-30 minutes until a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean. Cool completely on wire racks.
For the frosting, beat the cream cheese and butter together until fluffy, then gradually add powdered sugar and beat until smooth.
Frost the top of one layer, stack the second layer on top, and frost the top and sides generously.
